chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, that he said:

Regarding the man who cultivates on a sharing basis, so he farms someone else’s land, saying, 'A third is for the oxen, and a third for the sowing, and a third for the land.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not mention anything from the seeds, and the cows, but he should be saying, 'Cultivate such and such therein, if you so desire to, for a half, and if you so desire to, for a third'.
ai.seo_question: What is the correct way to structure a sharecropping contract in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the validity of *muzara'ah* (sharecropping) by prohibiting the specification of fixed shares for specific inputs like seeds or oxen, instead requiring the division of the total produce itself. This distinction ensures the contract avoids *gharar* (uncertainty) regarding the quality and quantity of individual components, aligning with Shia juristic principles that prioritize the division of the harvest over the division of the means of production. The ruling allows flexibility in the ratio (e.g., half or third), reflecting the practical economic arrangements of early Islamic agrarian society.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, 
from Abdullah Bin Sinan having said

regarding the man who cultivated on a sharing basis, so he farmed someone else’s land, ‘A third is for the oxen (ploughing), and a third for the sowing, and a third for the land’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should not mention anything from the seeds, and the cows, but he should be saying, ‘I shall cultivate such and such therein, if you so desire to, for a half, and if you so desire to, for a third’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al- Nadr ibn Suwayd from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “

About the case of a man who works in sharecropping, cultivates the land of another man and says, ‘One third for the bulls, one-third for the seed and one-third for the land’, he (the Imam) Alayhi al- Salam, has said, ‘Things like bulls, seeds and so on must not be mentioned, instead he must say, “You must cultivate so and so items, if you want for one-half or if you want for one-third.’””
